update_triggers: a model, field, upload, export, log, backup, secret, or client-storage surface changes
a protection control or retention period changes
an external service, data recipient, deployment model, or integration is added
the product enters a new jurisdiction or regulated, commercial, employment, health, or minors context
a privacy request, security finding, or incident changes the classification or handling requirements

current_context: private self-hosted budgeting for one invited household
no bank synchronization, payment processing, credit reporting, advertising, analytics, or sale of data
no public registration, commercial customer relationship, employer use, healthcare use, or designed use by minors
deployment and data custody remain with the household release owner except for the named infrastructure providers
baseline_commitments: household-scoped least-privilege access with recent authentication for the most sensitive actions
confidential transport, protected storage, bounded retention, and secure disposal according to classification
no sensitive data in URLs, telemetry, untrusted recipients, or ordinary application logs
documented export, correction, recovery, incident, and operator-led removal procedures
regulatory_and_privacy_scope.formal_determination: This engineering inventory does not claim a legal exemption or replace jurisdiction-specific advice. Before each deployment, the release owner records the deployment jurisdiction and confirms applicable privacy, breach-notification, financial-data, tax-record, provider-contract, and household obligations; the stricter documented baseline applies even when no named regulatory regime is triggered.
not_in_scope_yet: financial-institution, payment-card processor, consumer-reporting, investment-adviser, employer, healthcare, school, or child-directed processing
multi-tenant software as a service, public registration, behavioral analytics, advertising, data brokerage, or automated financial decisions
open-banking credentials, bank API payloads, payment instruments, government identifiers, biometrics, health data, or precise location history
reassessment_triggers: bank, payment, credit, tax, identity-provider, analytics, telemetry, messaging, or cloud-storage integration
processing for another household, an employer, a minor, or a regulated professional service
a new deployment jurisdiction, external data recipient, data-residency change, or provider-contract change
regulatory_and_privacy_scope.data_subject_process: Authenticated members may review and correct current household records and create protected financial or audit exports. Access or removal requests that are not supported in-product are handled by the household release owner using a verified offline procedure, encrypted backup and incident-hold constraints, and an audit-preserving record of the decision; append-only audit history is never silently rewritten.

protection_levels.name: Public
protection_levels.definition: Content intentionally safe for unauthenticated distribution and containing no household, identity, authentication, financial, security-sensitive, or deployment-specific values.
protection_levels.encryption_in_transit: Public application assets inherit the deployment HTTPS requirement even though confidentiality is not required; source downloads and release artifacts use authenticated HTTPS.
protection_levels.encryption_at_rest: Confidentiality encryption is not required, but reviewed source and built assets remain in access-controlled source and image storage.
protection_levels.database_level_encryption: Public data is not stored in the application database; if that changes, it inherits the database protections of the containing record.
protection_levels.integrity: Changes require source review, quality checks, and immutable or digest-pinned release artifacts.
protection_levels.retention: Retain only for the supported source and release lifecycle; remove obsolete assets through reviewed repository and image-retention processes.
protection_levels.logging: Names and fixed paths may appear in operational diagnostics, but request-derived content is not made public by classification.
protection_levels.log_access: Ordinary operator access is sufficient because logs must not gain sensitive values from this level transition.
protection_levels.access_control: Read access may be unauthenticated only for an explicitly reviewed public route or static asset; modification remains release-owner controlled.
protection_levels.privacy: No personal or household data is permitted; accessibility and ordinary non-tracking delivery remain required.
protection_levels.confidentiality: No confidentiality claim applies to the published bytes, but private hostnames and deployment details remain excluded.
protection_levels.encoding_and_masking: Encoding, compression, hashing, truncation, or masking does not lower classification; derived representations inherit the source level unless an approved irreversible declassification review proves otherwise.
protection_levels.disposal: Remove unsupported copies from release and source distribution; no special media sanitization is required when the no-sensitive-data rule is satisfied.
protection_levels.backup_and_recovery: Recovery relies on reviewed source and immutable build inputs rather than inclusion in household-data backups.
protection_levels.client_storage: Immutable versioned static assets may use ordinary browser caching; authenticated or household-derived content can never enter this level.

protection_levels.name: Internal
protection_levels.definition: Non-public operational, authorization-schema, dependency, or synthetic security information that does not contain live household or reusable credential data but could assist misuse or confuse a release if altered.
protection_levels.encryption_in_transit: Use authenticated encrypted transport outside one trusted host; do not send to an unlisted service or user-controlled destination.
protection_levels.encryption_at_rest: Store only in access-controlled source, image, host, or CI storage; host and provider encryption are required when the selected platform supports them.
protection_levels.database_level_encryption: Internal authorization metadata stored in PostgreSQL inherits the protected database volume requirement and must be included in release verification.
protection_levels.integrity: Require reviewed source, pinned dependencies, immutable artifacts, checksums or signatures where supplied, and least-privilege modification rights.
protection_levels.retention: Keep only for its operational, release, or evidence purpose and the documented provider lifecycle; remove stale local test output after review.
protection_levels.logging: May log bounded identifiers, versions, counts, and outcomes; never promote live sensitive values into internal logs.
protection_levels.log_access: Limit non-public operational logs to the release owner and administrators or the reviewed CI project.
protection_levels.access_control: Use repository, CI, host, and database-role permissions appropriate to the artifact; publication requires explicit declassification review.
protection_levels.privacy: Use synthetic fixtures and coarse operational values; exclude live identity, financial, behavioral, and network-address data.
protection_levels.confidentiality: Do not publish deployment topology, private hostnames, detailed findings before remediation, or reusable operational identifiers.
protection_levels.encoding_and_masking: Encoded, hashed, compressed, truncated, or masked derivatives inherit the source classification and may not be treated as declassified by format alone.
protection_levels.disposal: Delete expired local and provider artifacts through the documented platform process and verify sensitive source data was never embedded.
protection_levels.backup_and_recovery: Recover from reviewed source, provider artifacts within retention, or the encrypted deployment backup when the item is database-resident.
protection_levels.client_storage: Do not persist internal data in browser storage; transient display follows the authenticated no-store boundary when shown in the application.

protection_levels.name: Confidential
protection_levels.definition: Household identity, membership, security-event, notification, or pseudonymous operational data whose unauthorized disclosure could expose private behavior or help target an account.
protection_levels.encryption_in_transit: Require authenticated TLS on every TCP hop and a reviewed local Unix or filesystem boundary for same-host transfer; no plaintext LAN or public hop is allowed.
protection_levels.encryption_at_rest: Require access-controlled storage on an encrypted host volume, encrypted off-host backups, protected provider storage where applicable, and no unmanaged copies.
protection_levels.database_level_encryption: PostgreSQL storage must reside on an administrator-verified encrypted host volume; field encryption is added when the threat model requires separation from the database role. This remains a dated release verification item.
protection_levels.integrity: Use database constraints and transactions, protected audit events for security-relevant changes, validated structured logging, and signed checkpoints where the record participates in audit history.
protection_levels.retention: Apply the dataset-specific minimum and maximum, incident holds, and verified deletion or anonymization when the purpose ends; avoid indefinite convenience copies.
protection_levels.logging: Log only stable event names, coarse outcomes, counts, and pseudonymous identifiers. Exclude emails, names, addresses, free text, query strings, bodies, and full object values.
protection_levels.log_access: Limit protected logs to the isolated collector and Linux administrators; household audit views remain household-scoped and require recent authentication for detailed access and export.
protection_levels.access_control: Require authenticated household scope or a purpose-bound administrator/service identity, least-privilege database roles, MFA for members, and recent authentication for sensitive actions.
protection_levels.privacy: Minimize collection and linkability, avoid IP or detailed device fingerprint retention, support review/correction, and route removal requests through the verified household process.
protection_levels.confidentiality: Never place values in URLs, analytics, public artifacts, source control, ordinary logs, or an unlisted external service; screenshots and support evidence must be sanitized.
protection_levels.encoding_and_masking: Base64, URL encoding, hashing, pseudonymization, partial display, truncation, and other reversible or linkable transformations inherit the source classification.
protection_levels.disposal: Scrub expired working data, remove retired provider and host copies, and account for encrypted backup expiry and incident holds before claiming erasure.
protection_levels.backup_and_recovery: Include authoritative records only in encrypted Restic backups with documented retention and tested restoration; keep repository credentials separate from application access.
protection_levels.client_storage: Use secure HttpOnly cookies only where needed, no-store responses, no sensitive Web Storage or IndexedDB, and clear authenticated DOM and origin storage on termination.

protection_levels.name: Restricted
protection_levels.definition: Authentication secrets, cryptographic material, detailed financial records, raw imports, exports, backups, or audit payloads whose disclosure or alteration could enable account takeover, material privacy harm, or financial harm.
protection_levels.encryption_in_transit: Require authenticated TLS with exact peer validation on every network hop; internal service traffic uses purpose-separated mutual TLS and restricted data has no external application destination.
protection_levels.encryption_at_rest: Require an encrypted host volume, encrypted off-host backups, least-privilege file modes, and purpose-specific application encryption for recoverable authentication seeds or equivalent high-impact secrets.
protection_levels.database_level_encryption: PostgreSQL storage must reside on an administrator-verified encrypted host volume in addition to MFA seed field encryption and encrypted backups. Dated release verification must record encryption and key-custody evidence before V14.2.4 can be verified.
protection_levels.integrity: Require transactional invariants and constraints, append-only hash-chained audit history for material changes, independently signed checkpoints, authenticated encryption or keyed hashes for secrets, and restore-time integrity checks.
protection_levels.retention: Use the shortest dataset-specific period: authentication artifacts expire or rotate, raw import cells are scrubbed after 24 hours by default and never beyond 720 hours, exports are response-only, and durable financial/audit records follow the household retention decision plus legal or incident holds.
protection_levels.logging: Never log plaintext or encoded credentials, TOTP seeds, recovery codes, cookies, CSRF values, raw import cells, financial amounts, free-text financial details, export rows, backup contents, or cryptographic material.
protection_levels.log_access: Only redacted event metadata may enter protected logs; collector access is isolated from the application and limited to Linux administrators, while detailed audit access is household-scoped and recently reauthenticated.
protection_levels.access_control: Require authenticated household scope, MFA, recent authentication for exports and security actions, purpose-specific service and database identities, protected secret mounts, and separation of web, backup, restore, migration, integrity, and collector capabilities.
protection_levels.privacy: Collect only product-required values, avoid third-party disclosure and tracking, provide controlled exports, preserve correction history through append-only audit, and handle deletion against active storage, backups, checkpoints, and incident holds.
protection_levels.confidentiality: Never expose through URLs, logs, source control, CI artifacts, public documentation, screenshots, telemetry, client storage, or user-controlled destinations; sanitized evidence must use synthetic data.
protection_levels.encoding_and_masking: Ciphertext, password hashes, keyed pseudonyms, Base64 strings, QR payloads, signed session data, partial account numbers, compressed dumps, and masked values inherit restricted classification unless a documented irreversible declassification review says otherwise.
protection_levels.disposal: Use application scrubbing for staged data, cryptographic retirement for encrypted copies, secure secret-file replacement, session invalidation, provider artifact deletion, and documented media or deployment retirement; never claim deletion while retained backups remain live.
protection_levels.backup_and_recovery: Use encrypted Restic snapshots with separated credentials, 7 daily/4 weekly/12 monthly retention by default, quarterly restore rehearsal, signed audit comparison, and no restore over the live database.
protection_levels.client_storage: Keep only opaque secure HttpOnly session and CSRF cookies as required; sensitive responses are no-store/private, financial data stays out of browser databases and Web Storage, and termination clears origin storage and authenticated DOM.

datasets.name: Authentication, MFA, recovery, throttling, and session material
datasets.scope: Stored and transient values used to establish, recover, limit, or revoke an authenticated identity.
data_elements: password hashes and password submissions
encrypted TOTP seeds, enrollment QR payloads, and one-time codes
recovery-code hashes and submitted recovery codes
opaque session keys, signed server-side session payloads, CSRF values, and recent-authentication timestamps
keyed login-throttle pseudonyms, failure counts, and lockout times
datasets.created_or_processed: Created during bootstrap, login, MFA enrollment, recovery, reauthentication, password change, session rotation, and throttling; raw secrets are processed only for the immediate operation.
datasets.storage: Password and recovery values are one-way hashed, TOTP seeds are authenticated-encrypted with a separate mounted key, and sessions are server-side database records with only opaque browser cookies.
datasets.transit: Submitted only in HTTPS bodies and protected cookies over the exact private hostname; no email, SMS, analytics, or third-party authentication transport exists.
datasets.integrity: Django hash verification, authenticated seed encryption, atomic key rotation, single-use recovery records, session versioning, and protected audit events cover security changes.
datasets.retention: Raw submissions and displayed recovery values are not retained; sessions expire within 12 hours and on browser close or revocation; hashes and encrypted seeds remain until reset, rotation, account removal, or deployment retirement.
datasets.logging: Credentials, submitted identifiers, codes, cookies, session keys, and seed material are prohibited; only coarse event names, outcomes, pseudonymous context, and bounded counts are allowed.
datasets.log_access: Redacted security records go to the isolated archive; members see only household-scoped audit events, with recent password-plus-MFA confirmation for detailed access and export.
datasets.access_control: Only the identity owner and purpose-bound identity services may use the material; emergency resets require the authenticated host administrator and revoke sessions.
datasets.privacy: The application retains no IP address or detailed device fingerprint, recovery responses conceal account existence, and active-session references are keyed opaque values.
datasets.disposal: Reset deletes MFA and recovery records, password changes and administrative actions revoke sessions, rotation retires prior keys, and deployment retirement removes encrypted backups according to their schedule.

datasets.name: Framework authorization and content-type schema
datasets.scope: Django permission, group, and content-type records that describe authorization capabilities rather than household data.
data_elements: permission names and codenames
group membership schema
installed application and model identifiers
datasets.created_or_processed: Created by reviewed migrations and administrator actions; not accepted through public registration.
datasets.storage: Stored in PostgreSQL with the same encrypted-volume requirement and backup boundary as application records.
datasets.transit: Used only inside authenticated Django and database connections protected by the private HTTPS and mutual-TLS boundaries.
datasets.integrity: Migration review, framework constraints, administrative audit, and purpose-specific database roles prevent unreviewed mutation.
datasets.retention: Retained while the corresponding application capability exists and removed only through reviewed migrations or deployment retirement.
datasets.logging: Permission identifiers and coarse authorization outcomes may be logged; actor identity and household context stay pseudonymous in operational logs.
datasets.log_access: Operational and security log access is limited to administrators and the isolated collector boundary.
datasets.access_control: Only authenticated framework code, migrations, and authorized administrators may read or change schema records.
datasets.privacy: Group assignment can reveal role relationships, so live assignments are not published even though schema names are internal rather than financial.
datasets.disposal: Use reviewed migrations and database retirement; verify stale permissions are not left active after feature removal.

datasets.name: Household profile and membership data
datasets.scope: Names, email-linked membership, household preferences, currency, time zone, and active membership relationships.
data_elements: household name, currency, and time zone
member email and display name contained in the restricted user record
membership state and join time
datasets.created_or_processed: Created through trusted bootstrap and maintained by authenticated household workflows.
datasets.storage: Stored in PostgreSQL and encrypted backups; user identity fields remain in the higher restricted authentication dataset.
datasets.transit: Rendered only over private HTTPS and exchanged with PostgreSQL over purpose-bound mutual TLS.
datasets.integrity: Foreign keys, uniqueness constraints, transactional services, and protected membership audit events preserve relationships.
datasets.retention: Retained for the active household and its audit/accounting continuity; removal is an operator-led verified process that accounts for backups and audit holds.
datasets.logging: Names and email addresses are excluded from application logs; pseudonymous actor and household identifiers support correlation.
datasets.log_access: Only redacted metadata enters administrator or collector logs; household audit access remains scoped and recently authenticated where required.
datasets.access_control: Active authenticated membership gates every household object; MFA, session controls, and object-level household queries prevent cross-household access.
datasets.privacy: Collect only identity and localization values needed to operate the private household; do not retain IP addresses or detailed fingerprints.
datasets.disposal: Deactivate access first, revoke sessions, then use the verified owner process for active data and scheduled encrypted-backup expiry.

datasets.name: Household budgeting, income, spending, debt, goal, reserve, notification, and import records
datasets.scope: The complete authoritative financial planning and ledger dataset, including raw staged statement rows and derived projections.
data_elements: account names, types, last four digits, balances, notes, receipts, categories, and journal entries
income and expense schedules, dates, amounts, adjustments, pay periods, and reconciliation state
debt balances, rates, fees, terms, statements, mortgage components, and payoff plans
goal targets, dates, contributions, funding rules, and reserve allocations
uploaded filenames, checksums, raw CSV cells, mappings, duplicate fingerprints, and validation outcomes
notification content, preferences, due dates, and read or dismissal state
datasets.created_or_processed: Created by authenticated forms, bounded CSV staging, deterministic financial services, notification evaluation, and reviewed maintenance tasks; projections and summaries remain restricted derivatives.
datasets.storage: Stored in PostgreSQL, encrypted Restic backups, and append-only audit before/after payloads; raw upload bytes are parsed in memory and never stored as files.
datasets.transit: Private HTTPS to approved household browsers and purpose-bound mutual TLS to PostgreSQL; no bank, analytics, telemetry, email, or external application destination exists.
datasets.integrity: Decimal arithmetic, database constraints, row locks, idempotency keys, immutable revisions, double-entry invariants, protected audit events, and signed checkpoints protect material changes.
datasets.retention: Durable records follow the household accounting and legal retention decision; raw staged cells are scrubbed after 24 hours by default and never beyond 720 hours; superseded values remain in protected history rather than being silently rewritten.
datasets.logging: Financial amounts, names, notes, raw rows, filters, queries, and notification content are prohibited; only event type, pseudonymous IDs, row counts, and coarse outcomes are allowed.
datasets.log_access: Redacted event metadata is isolated in the security archive; full before/after history is available only through household-scoped, recently authenticated audit access.
datasets.access_control: Every query and mutation is household-scoped; sensitive exports and audit detail require recent authentication; database identities are separated by runtime and maintenance purpose.
datasets.privacy: No trackers or external synchronizers receive the data; partial account numbers are for household recognition and remain restricted rather than declassified.
datasets.disposal: Abandoned raw imports are scrubbed automatically; durable record and backup removal requires the verified owner process, documented retention decision, and audit-preserving treatment.

datasets.name: Protected audit history, checkpoints, and framework administration history
datasets.scope: Security- and finance-relevant before/after history, actor relationships, hash-chain state, signatures, and administrative representations.
data_elements: audit actions, entity identifiers, reasons, actor and household links, request identifiers, and before/after payloads
sequence numbers, event hashes, chain heads, verification times, checkpoint signatures, key identifiers, and external filenames
framework administrator action time, target representation, flag, and change description
datasets.created_or_processed: Appended for material financial, identity, import, export, recovery, and maintenance actions; checkpoint files are created only after full chain verification.
datasets.storage: Append-only PostgreSQL audit schema plus a separate protected checkpoint mount; encrypted backups retain database history.
datasets.transit: Household audit pages and CSV exports use private HTTPS; integrity services reach PostgreSQL through their purpose-bound mutual-TLS identity.
datasets.integrity: Canonical event serialization, SHA-256 chaining, database append controls, full-chain verification, and independently keyed HMAC checkpoints make unauthorized changes detectable.
datasets.retention: Retain for the lifetime of the financial history and applicable incident, accounting, or legal holds; never silently delete or rewrite events to satisfy an ordinary edit.
datasets.logging: Full payloads, reasons, and object representations are prohibited from operational logs; only coarse action, counts, pseudonymous context, and integrity outcome are allowed.
datasets.log_access: Detailed application audit access is household-scoped and recently authenticated; external checkpoint and operational log access is limited to purpose-bound services and administrators.
datasets.access_control: Runtime code appends through controlled services but cannot update or delete history; integrity readers and signing writers are separately scoped.
datasets.privacy: Exports are explicit sensitive events; correction history is preserved while disclosure and removal requests are resolved through a documented audit-preserving owner process.
datasets.disposal: Checkpoint and audit removal occurs only with documented deployment retirement or a controlling legal decision, including encrypted backups and incident holds.

datasets.name: Transient request, form, upload, template, and response values
datasets.scope: Sensitive values processed in application or proxy memory without becoming a distinct persistent record.
data_elements: form submissions, passwords, one-time codes, search text, filters, and CSRF values
raw bounded CSV upload bytes and parsed cells
rendered financial, identity, notification, and audit values
temporary QR and recovery-code enrollment output
datasets.created_or_processed: Exists only while nginx, Gunicorn, Django, template rendering, streaming export, or the approved browser handles one request.
datasets.storage: No request-body cache or upload file is retained by the product; bounded uploads remain in memory and selected values become classified database records only after validation.
datasets.transit: HTTPS and internal mutual TLS only, with sensitive inputs in message bodies or protected headers rather than URLs.
datasets.integrity: Request framing controls, CSRF, validation, canonical parsing, transactional writes, contextual output encoding, and CSP protect interpretation.
datasets.retention: Discard after request completion except for explicitly validated classified records, protected audit metadata, and streamed downloads controlled by the recipient.
datasets.logging: Bodies, query text, sensitive headers, exception messages, raw paths, and rendered values are prohibited from logs.
datasets.log_access: Only redacted event metadata and code-location diagnostics may reach administrator or collector logs.
datasets.access_control: Authentication, household scope, MFA, recent authentication, CSRF, and purpose-specific endpoints gate processing.
datasets.privacy: Data is minimized to the requested operation and never copied to analytics, remote error reporting, or telemetry.
datasets.disposal: Release request references promptly; do not retain debug captures, screenshots, or proxy dumps unless sanitized evidence procedures apply.

datasets.name: Approved-browser cookies, DOM, storage, and cache surface
datasets.scope: Opaque authentication cookies and transient authenticated content on an approved household device.
data_elements: opaque session and CSRF cookies
rendered authenticated DOM and form state
non-sensitive theme preference
browser cache, history, screenshots, and downloaded artifacts under user control
datasets.created_or_processed: Created during private authenticated browsing and removed or expired at session termination; only the light or dark theme value is intentionally persisted in Web Storage.
datasets.storage: Secure host-only Strict HttpOnly cookies carry opaque values; authenticated responses are no-store/private and financial data is not written to Web Storage, IndexedDB, or Cache Storage.
datasets.transit: Exact private Tailscale HTTPS hostname only, with same-origin CSP, CSRF, referrer, opener, framing, and cross-origin response controls.
datasets.integrity: Signed server-side session state, cookie attributes, CSP, contextual output encoding, and same-origin controls protect the surface.
datasets.retention: Cookies expire at browser close or within 12 hours and are invalidated on revocation; authenticated DOM and origin storage are cleared on termination paths.
datasets.logging: Browser diagnostics are opt-in and temporary; cookies, DOM contents, storage values, and screenshots never enter ordinary logs or evidence.
datasets.log_access: Only the approved device user controls local diagnostics; sanitized test evidence follows release-owner access rules.
datasets.access_control: Device approval, Tailscale identity, application authentication, MFA, session timeout, and recent authentication protect access.
datasets.privacy: No analytics, advertising, fingerprinting, service worker, or sensitive persistent browser database exists.
datasets.disposal: Logout and revoked-session behavior clears origin storage and authenticated DOM; the user must protect or delete screenshots and downloads outside product control.

datasets.name: Generated financial and audit CSV downloads
datasets.scope: Fresh response-only CSV representations of household transactions or protected audit history.
data_elements: transaction dates, descriptions, categories, accounts, amounts, notes, and provenance
audit timestamps, actions, actor display, entity identifiers, reasons, and before/after values
generated timestamped filenames
datasets.created_or_processed: Generated only after recent authentication, household scope, full audit-integrity verification where applicable, and a recorded export event.
datasets.storage: Streamed directly to the approved browser with no server-side export file or object-store copy.
datasets.transit: Private HTTPS with attachment disposition, no-store/private, and no-cache response headers.
datasets.integrity: CSV quoting, deterministic fields, spreadsheet-formula neutralization, household filters, and audit-chain verification protect generation.
datasets.retention: The server retains no export copy; recipient-managed files remain restricted and must follow the household retention and deletion decision.
datasets.logging: Rows, values, search text, and filenames are prohibited; only authorization outcome, export identifier, scope, and row count are recorded.
datasets.log_access: Redacted security metadata is isolated from application users; the export itself is available only to the recently authenticated household member.
datasets.access_control: Authenticated household membership and recent password-plus-MFA confirmation are mandatory; integrity failure blocks audit export.
datasets.privacy: The UI warns that downloaded files leave application controls; no third party receives a copy.
datasets.disposal: The recipient is responsible for encrypted storage and deletion of downloads; test outputs use synthetic data and are removed after validation.

datasets.name: Deployment secrets, private keys, certificates, and service credentials
datasets.scope: Reusable material that authenticates services, encrypts data, signs checkpoints, or controls private host access.
data_elements: Django signing and MFA encryption keys
Restic repository password and audit checkpoint signing key
PostgreSQL, Gunicorn, nginx, SSH, and Tailscale private identity material
database role credentials used only during isolated bootstrap or test boundaries
datasets.created_or_processed: Generated by an operating-system CSPRNG or reviewed provider, mounted only into exact consumers, and rotated through staged purpose-specific procedures.
datasets.storage: Root-owned secret files, provider-controlled protected state, and separately protected recovery copies; never environment values in production or repository content.
datasets.transit: Private keys and reusable secrets are not transmitted through application requests; certificates and protocol proofs use their designed authenticated channels.
datasets.integrity: File ownership and modes, certificate chains, exact consumers, key identifiers, staged rotation, negative tests, and inventory review prevent substitution or reuse.
datasets.retention: Retain only active and explicitly staged material; retire and destroy superseded keys after rotation evidence, except protected recovery material required to restore encrypted backups.
datasets.logging: Names, versions, fingerprints where approved, and outcomes only; actual or encoded material is categorically prohibited.
datasets.log_access: Operational rotation records are administrator-only and redacted; no secret value enters application or collector logs.
datasets.access_control: Root-owned files and read-only mounts expose each secret only to its purpose-bound service; the web container lacks backup, signing, bootstrap, and host-control secrets.
datasets.privacy: Separation limits the blast radius of a service compromise and prevents one key from linking unrelated protected datasets.
datasets.disposal: Securely replace files, recreate consumers, invalidate prior sessions or credentials, verify retired material fails, and remove transient generation artifacts.

datasets.name: Encrypted backup repository, restore streams, and recovery copies
datasets.scope: Encrypted snapshots and transient restore streams containing the full identity, financial, session, and audit database.
data_elements: PostgreSQL logical dump inside authenticated encrypted Restic packs
repository metadata, encrypted keys, snapshots, and integrity indexes
transient restore stream and restored verification database
non-sensitive last-success timestamp and release marker
datasets.created_or_processed: Created daily by the purpose-bound backup service and processed only by isolated backup, key-rotation, notification, and restore-verification roles.
datasets.storage: Existing off-VM mount with Restic authenticated encryption; repository password and database client identity remain separately mounted.
datasets.transit: Database dump and restore use mutually authenticated PostgreSQL connections and local mounted storage; the application has no remote backup transport.
datasets.integrity: Restic authentication and repository checks, digest-pinned images, restore rehearsal, migration checks, audit-chain verification, and signed external checkpoints protect recovery.
datasets.retention: Seven daily, four weekly, and twelve monthly snapshots by default, with incident holds overriding normal expiry and quarterly restoration evidence required.
datasets.logging: Only fixed event names, release identifiers, timestamps, snapshot metadata, counts, and outcomes; dump content, repository secrets, and financial data are prohibited.
datasets.log_access: Repository access is limited to purpose-bound maintenance identities and administrators; the web and notification services cannot read backup contents.
datasets.access_control: Separate database certificates, read-only consumer mounts, networkless key rotation, pre-existing host paths, and no Docker socket in containers enforce least privilege.
datasets.privacy: Backups inherit every source record's highest classification; encryption does not declassify them, and removal claims account for retained snapshots.
datasets.disposal: Apply reviewed Restic forget/prune retention, retire repository keys through staged rotation, destroy obsolete recovery copies, and remove disposable restore databases after exact-target verification.

datasets.name: Application, security, service, host, provider, and CI logs
datasets.scope: Redacted diagnostic and security-event metadata across all 14 inventoried stack layers.
data_elements: timestamps, event names, levels, releases, methods, route names, counts, and outcomes
pseudonymous request, actor, household, import, export, and entity identifiers
code locations without exception text and fixed service lifecycle messages
provider connection and CI job metadata subject to the documented limitations
datasets.created_or_processed: Created by reviewed application log calls, the isolated collector, infrastructure services, systemd, Tailscale, security tests, and CI.
datasets.storage: Bounded Docker local storage, collector-only archive volume, host journal, provider systems, and reviewed CI artifacts according to the logging inventory.
datasets.transit: Local process streams, permission-restricted Unix datagrams, host-local journal capture, and provider-authenticated HTTPS; no application log shipper has external egress.
datasets.integrity: Structured JSON encoding, allowlisted fields, central redaction, collector revalidation, append-only writes, fixed event catalogs, and audit correlation limit injection and tampering.
datasets.retention: Docker stores at most about 100 MiB per container, the isolated security archive has a 90-day minimum, CI uses reviewed provider retention, and incident holds supersede deletion.
datasets.logging: This dataset is itself the only approved log representation; raw credentials, identities, request data, financial values, free text, and exception messages remain prohibited.
datasets.log_access: Collector and host records are Linux-administrator-only, CI records are repository-role controlled, and Tailscale provider access is limited to approved administrators.
datasets.access_control: The application can write but cannot read or alter the isolated archive; provider and host access follows individually authenticated administrator roles.
datasets.privacy: Pseudonymization, exclusion of IP addresses and detailed fingerprints, no optional flow logging by default, and explicit evidence sanitization minimize linkability.
datasets.disposal: Use documented rotation and provider deletion, verify oldest retained timestamps, and preserve only sanitized decision evidence after the operational need ends.

datasets.name: Source, CI, scan, test, and release evidence
datasets.scope: Reviewed code, generated inventories, synthetic test output, scan findings, and sanitized release decisions.
data_elements: source code, migrations, configuration templates, dependency locks, and generated manifests
synthetic fixtures, test outcomes, coverage, SBOM, vulnerability, browser, restore, and network-boundary results
sanitized findings, release identifiers, verification dates, and reviewer decisions
datasets.created_or_processed: Created in trusted development and GitHub Actions from reviewed source and synthetic data; live household data is prohibited.
datasets.storage: Access-controlled repository, developer workspace, immutable workflow artifacts, and sanitized committed evidence.
datasets.transit: Authenticated HTTPS and Git/SSH to the reviewed repository; no release workflow receives production data or secrets beyond platform-scoped ephemeral credentials.
datasets.integrity: Pull-request review, immutable action pins, dependency hashes, image digests, deterministic generators, checksums, and required checks protect decisions.
datasets.retention: Provider artifacts follow the documented 90-day target; durable sanitized evidence remains with the supported release history; local unsanitized output is deleted after review.
datasets.logging: Synthetic values and bounded tool output only; secrets, private hostnames, live addresses, and household data are prohibited and secret-scanned.
datasets.log_access: Repository and CI permissions limit non-public findings to maintainers until remediation and approved disclosure.
datasets.access_control: Trusted contributors and reviewed automation only; release evidence changes require source review and validator agreement.
datasets.privacy: Use synthetic fixtures, redact screenshots and logs, and never upload real household exports, databases, cookies, or identifiers.
datasets.disposal: Remove temporary contexts, containers, volumes, artifacts, and local captures after evidence is summarized and retention expires.

datasets.name: Offline breached-password reference corpus
datasets.scope: A reviewed hash-only subset of publicly breached password SHA-1 identifiers used solely for local blocklist membership.
data_elements: uppercase fixed-length SHA-1 password hashes without counts or plaintext
corpus version, source label, build date, entry count, and checksum
datasets.created_or_processed: Built by a trusted maintainer from the official downloaded corpus outside application runtime and packaged as a bounded immutable artifact.
datasets.storage: Read-only application package data and reviewed source artifact; transient source downloads remain outside the repository and are deleted after validation.
datasets.transit: The production application never contacts the source service; maintainers use authenticated HTTPS through the official downloader outside runtime.
datasets.integrity: Strict parser, exact ordering and uniqueness, metadata schema, minimum size and freshness, bounded bytes, checksum, and fail-closed hardened startup.
datasets.retention: Replace within 180 days and delete the transient full source immediately after the packaged subset and checksum are verified.
datasets.logging: Only corpus version, entry count, build date, checksum outcome, and validation error category; candidate passwords and hashes are prohibited.
datasets.log_access: Build output is maintainer-only until the reviewed hash artifact is committed; application validation emits no corpus entries.
datasets.access_control: Trusted maintainer build path and read-only runtime package access; no end-user import, selection, or destination exists.
datasets.privacy: No application password, account identity, occurrence count, or plaintext is included; hash format does not make password guesses safe to disclose as user data.
datasets.disposal: Delete downloaded source and temporary chunks after atomic output; replace stale packaged corpus through reviewed source control.

datasets.name: Release, readiness, backup-freshness, and service-health metadata
datasets.scope: Coarse non-secret values needed to run and observe the private deployment without exposing application records.
data_elements: release identifier, environment label, timestamps, counts, exit state, and health outcome
backup last-success marker without repository content
minimal liveness response and internal readiness state
container, timer, certificate-expiry, and storage-capacity status
datasets.created_or_processed: Created by release automation, maintenance services, probes, and host supervision.
datasets.storage: Environment configuration, mode-0600 marker, bounded logs, host journal, and sanitized release evidence.
datasets.transit: Health responses are limited to the exact private boundary; host and CI status uses authenticated administrative channels.
datasets.integrity: Exact allowlists, fixed formats, atomic marker replacement, purpose-bound writers, and release-evidence validation protect state.
datasets.retention: Keep current operational state and bounded history needed for release, alert, capacity, and incident decisions; delete stale diagnostic captures.
datasets.logging: Coarse values are allowed, but paths, hostnames, addresses, credentials, and record content remain prohibited.
datasets.log_access: Host and CI roles limit non-public status; household users receive only minimal in-application notification state.
datasets.access_control: Purpose-bound service identities and authenticated administrators write or inspect operational state; public monitoring endpoints are absent.
datasets.privacy: Health and freshness features deliberately avoid member identity, activity details, and financial content.
datasets.disposal: Rotate bounded logs and obsolete markers, sanitize retained release decisions, and remove deployment metadata at host retirement.

datasets.name: Intentionally public static presentation assets
datasets.scope: Reviewed CSS and JavaScript necessary to render the login and authenticated interfaces, without embedded household or deployment values.
data_elements: versioned CSS presentation rules
dependency-free JavaScript for theme, storage cleanup, and fixed form behavior
datasets.created_or_processed: Authored and reviewed in source, compressed into the immutable application image, and served by WhiteNoise.
datasets.storage: Repository and immutable release image only; no runtime user content is written into static files.
datasets.transit: Served over the same exact private HTTPS origin, with same-origin cross-origin resource policy and CSP.
datasets.integrity: Source review, native-client inventory, output-safety scan, static manifest hashing, immutable image, and browser tests protect changes.
datasets.retention: Retain with supported releases and remove obsolete image and source versions through release lifecycle management.
datasets.logging: Fixed asset paths and response status may be logged; query strings, referrers, identities, and response bytes remain excluded.
datasets.log_access: Ordinary administrator operational access applies because the assets themselves contain no sensitive data.
datasets.access_control: Assets may be read without application authentication but are reachable only through the private ingress; modification requires reviewed source and release access.
datasets.privacy: No tracker, analytics identifier, fingerprinting logic, personal data, or external asset request is permitted.
datasets.disposal: Remove unsupported release images and source versions according to repository and host retention.
